tasks.short: Decide the day's feeding, treatment and cleaning assignments, write them on the board, brief workers, and check the tasks are done.

steps.what: Farm supervisor decides the day's assignments for feeding, treatment and cleaning of animal quarters
Farm supervisor writes the day's task list: on the whiteboard and paper sheets today; after the change adjusts the tasks the app generates from the schedules
Farm supervisor checks the day's task list: every pen and tank covered, treatments match the vet's plan, and each task has a worker
Farm supervisor publishes the checked task list to the workers' phones
Farm supervisor assigns tasks to workers at the morning briefing
Workers tick each task off on their phone when it is done
Farm supervisor checks that tasks are done: walks every pen today; after the change walks to open tasks and spot-checks done ones

tasks.design: Recurring feeding, treatment and cleaning tasks per pen or tank are generated each day from fixed schedules in a farm task app ({OPS_SYSTEM}); the supervisor adjusts them, checks the list and publishes it to the workers instead of writing the board and paper sheets. Workers tick tasks off on a phone, so the supervisor sees open tasks on one screen and walks round only for those. Deciding and briefing stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Task lists were written by hand each day and completion checked by walking round.
tasks.enabler_now: Task apps on phones generate recurring tasks and show what is still open.
tasks.still_hard: Sick animals change the day's plan at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which worker handles a nervous animal best.

reach.learn: Whether the day's tasks are clear.

evidence.claim: Task apps can generate recurring tasks from schedules and show open tasks per worker.
Task completion logged per worker can check performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the day plan to tasks checked; veterinary treatment plans are outside.
Input contract: recurring schedules set per pen or tank; fallback is the whiteboard.
Workers tick tasks off (s3w, share 1) in about the time reporting back took; this is outside the supervisor's savings.
Works council consent comes before tasks are logged per worker.

Deciding, briefing, checking and publishing the list keep their full time. s2 keeps 30 for adjusting the generated tasks. s4 keeps 60 because the supervisor still walks to open tasks and spot-checks the work done.

incremental.description: Farm supervisor keeps the recurring task schedules current.

approvals.approved_version: The day's task list with tasks, pens or tanks, treatments and workers exactly as checked by the supervisor in s2c, published once to the workers in the farm task app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small farm where the supervisor sees every task and few tasks recur (6.6); high: a large site with many pens and tanks (16.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count and weigh fish or shellfish, write counts on tank sheets, type them into the stock register, match sales and shipments, and check the monthly stock balance.

steps.what: Farm supervisor counts and weighs fish or shellfish reared, harvested and released
Farm supervisor records counts and types: on paper tank sheets today, on a tablet at the tank after the change
Farm supervisor types the tank sheets into the stock register spreadsheet
Farm supervisor records numbers sold and shipped from delivery notes
Farm supervisor checks the monthly stock balance and explains differences

tasks.design: Counts, weights, species and mortality are entered on a tablet at the tank in the farm management software ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which keeps the stock register per tank, so tank sheets are not written and typed in later. Sales and shipments are booked from the delivery notes in the sales system ({ERP}) into the register, so the supervisor does not copy them by hand. Counting fish and explaining stock differences stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts were written on paper, typed into a spreadsheet and sales copied from delivery notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Farm management software keeps stock per tank and takes sales from the sales system.
tasks.still_hard: Counts at harvest are estimates from sample weights.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a tank's numbers do not match what is in the water.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor checks stock instead of copying numbers.

reach.learn: Whether stock per tank is current.

evidence.claim: Farm management software can keep stock per tank and take sales from a sales system.
Aquaculture farms must keep records of stock movements and mortality under animal health rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock movement to the balance checked; pricing is outside.
Input contract: tanks and species set up; fallback is tank sheets.
Entering on a tablet takes about as long as writing on paper, so s2 keeps its full time; typing the sheets in later (s3) goes. s4 keeps 30 for checking the booked sales against the notes.
Sales staff's time does not change.

incremental.description: Farm supervisor corrects entries that do not match delivery notes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tablets fail at wet tanks, so about half the sheets are still typed in (19.5); high: counts entered at the tank (29.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk the site and observe workers, warn those breaking safety rules, write the warning note, and decide discipline with HR.

steps.what: Farm supervisor monitors workers to ensure safety regulations are followed
Farm supervisor warns workers who violate safety regulations
Farm supervisor writes a note of the warning for the personnel file
Farm supervisor decides discipline for repeated breaches with HR

tasks.design: Warnings are recorded on a short phone form with the rule broken from a list, place, time and an optional photo, saved to the worker's file in the HR system ({HCM}), instead of a typed note. Earlier warnings show on the same file, so the supervisor and HR see repeated breaches without searching. Watching, warning and deciding discipline stay with the supervisor and HR. The warning note belongs to the personnel records task 45-1011.00:23362 and is priced there; observing, warning and deciding discipline do not change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Warnings were typed up later or not written down at all.
tasks.enabler_now: HR systems take short forms from a phone.
tasks.still_hard: Workers with little Dutch need the warning explained in person.
tasks.human_edge: Warning someone firmly without losing their trust.

evidence.claim: HR systems can take short forms from a phone and file them per employee.
Disciplinary decisions may not rest solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Boundary: from work in progress to discipline decided; dismissal procedures are outside.
Input contract: safety rules listed in the form; fallback is a typed note.
Watching and warning do not change.
s3 is part of keeping personnel action records, which sibling task 45-1011.00:23362 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.

incremental.description: No upkeep in this task; keeping the safety rule list current is counted with sibling task 45-1011.00:23362.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No saving in this task: the only changed step belongs to sibling task 45-1011.00:23362.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe animals on rounds, decide whether the vet or manager is needed, phone them, and record observations and treatments.

steps.what: Farm supervisor observes animals for signs of illness, injury or unusual behaviour
Farm supervisor decides whether the veterinarian or manager is needed
Farm supervisor phones the veterinarian or manager
Farm supervisor records observations, deaths and treatments: in the paper logbook today, on a phone per pen or tank after the change

tasks.design: Observations, deaths and treatments are recorded per pen or tank on a phone in the farm management software ({OPS_SYSTEM}) by picking the sign from a list and adding a photo where useful, instead of writing the paper logbook. Recording takes as long as the logbook; the gain is that the vet sees the same record before a visit. Observing animals, deciding and phoning the vet stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations were written in a logbook that the vet saw only on site.
tasks.enabler_now: Farm software on phones records signs and treatments per pen or tank.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual signs do not fit the list.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that an animal is off before it shows clear signs.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in time; the vet sees the record before a visit.

reach.learn: Whether history is available before a visit.

evidence.claim: Farm software on phones can record signs, deaths and treatments per pen or tank.
Farms must keep records of medicines given to food-producing animals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the animal round to observations recorded; treatment by the vet is outside.
Input contract: pens, tanks and sign lists set up; fallback is the logbook.
Observing, deciding, phoning and recording keep their full time: picking a sign from a list is not faster than writing it.
The vet's time does not change.
unknowns: Pens or tanks on the round.

incremental.description: No upkeep: notes for signs not on the list are part of recording in s4, and the sign lists are set up once.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No saving: observing, deciding and phoning stay in person, and recording on the phone takes as long as the logbook (0.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The farm supervisor keeps deciding assignments, counting stock, watching safety and observing animals; whiteboards, tank sheets, typed registers and paper logbooks shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using farm software on a phone
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor with more time with animals and crew.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
